headline: Researchers used AI to make mRNA vaccines that could stay stable at room temperature, in early mouse tests.
score_reason: Early mouse results in a journal report, relayed by Reuters; no human trials reported.
importance_line: It could mean mRNA vaccines that do not need ultra-cold storage, which the researchers say could cut storage costs by up to 86 percent, but the results so far come only from mice.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Devdiscourse, that researchers used AI to make the tiny fatty particles that carry mRNA in vaccines more heat-resistant, so the vaccines could stay stable at room temperature for up to a year, according to a Nature Biotechnology report. The results are early and come from mice, whose immune responses matched those from vaccines using a formulation like Moderna's original.
notes: Reuters original blocked here (401). Read via Devdiscourse's copy of the Reuters Health Rounds item. Results are in mice; study leader Jinbi Tian of MIT (study leader at MIT, per Reuters).
